walkthroughs.body_html:
Choosing Strategic Direction — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Choosing Strategic Direction brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Choosing Strategic Direction.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How does HRM differ from traditional personnel management?
options: HRM treats people as a strategic asset and integrates human resource policies with business strategy; personnel management is more administrative and reactive, handling hiring, pay and disputes.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
HRM and personnel are exactly the same thing — just a name change.
HRM only applies to large multinational companies.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit?
options: HRM only applies to large multinational companies.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Gross profit = revenue minus cost of goods sold (direct costs only); net profit = revenue minus ALL costs including overheads, interest and tax. Net profit is the bottom line.
Gross profit and net profit are the same thing.

mcqs.q: What are Porter's two main generic strategies for competitive advantage?
options: Porter's strategies are about marketing channels.
Cost leadership (being the lowest-cost producer) and differentiation (offering unique value customers will pay more for) — Porter argues firms should choose one or the other.
Porter says businesses should pursue both low cost and differentiation at once.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
